title: This 245-Million-Year-Old Fossil Still Has Its Stomach Inside!
summary: Imagine finding a 245-million-year-old animal with its stomach still inside. That's exactly what scientists found in China! A fossil of a small sea reptile called Austronaga minuta is nearly complete — and it still has its stomach, liver and intestines. It's the oldest known example of a mostly complete digestive system in a reptile. The animal was only about 60 centimeters long — about the size of a school ruler. But its neck and tail were super long. Its long tail helped it swim, and its front legs were shaped like fins to steer. Here's the weird part: Austronaga was related to land reptiles like crocodiles and dinosaurs, not to famous sea reptiles like ichthyosaurs. Yet it still learned to live in the ocean. Scientists used UV light and special machines to study the dark spot between its ribs. They found a big stomach, a red liver, and a long tube for intestines. Unlike today's birds and crocodiles, which have two stomach parts, Austronaga had just one. This tells scientists that early reptiles had simple stomachs that got more complex later. The fossil is now in Beijing, and researchers hope to find more clues about how reptiles moved from land to sea.
why_it_matters: Studying fossils like this helps kids see that the animals alive today — including us — are the result of millions of years of slow changes, and that clues about the past are still being dug up right now.

background_read: Paleontologists (scientists who dig up and study ancient life) know that fossils usually form when an animal is quickly buried in mud or sand, and its hard bones slowly turn to stone.
Soft parts like stomachs almost never survive that process, which is why finding a 245-million-year-old stomach is such a surprise.
Beijing (the capital city of China) has large natural history museums and research centres where fossils like this one are cleaned, studied and put on show.
Article_Structure: WHO: Scientists studying a fossil reptile called Austronaga minuta, now kept in Beijing
WHAT: They found a nearly complete 245-million-year-old fossil that still has its stomach, liver and intestines inside
WHERE: In China, studied later in Beijing
WHY: It is the oldest known mostly complete digestive system in a reptile, and it shows early reptiles had simple one-part stomachs

perspectives.description: They think the fossil is amazing because soft organs almost never survive for 245 million years, so it gives a rare peek inside an ancient animal.
Some may say one fossil is only one clue, and they need to find more Austronaga fossils before they can be sure about how reptile stomachs changed.
People who see the fossil in Beijing get to imagine a small fin-legged reptile swimming in the sea long before dinosaurs were famous.
